payload.name: Extract explicit primary goals
payload.description: When a speaker explicitly states their number one goal, top priority, or primary aspiration (e.g., 'my number one goal is', 'I most want to'), extract it as a memory candidate during ingestion.
content: During candidate extraction, treat explicit first-person statements of a primary goal or top priority as high-importance memory candidates (e.g., preference or plan).
If a speaker uses superlative phrasing like 'number one goal', 'top priority', 'most important thing to me', or similar, capture the stated objective without requiring additional confirmation.

candidates.solves: Diagnosed cause: explicit first-person statements of a top priority (e.g., 'number one goal') were skipped during ingestion, causing later recall failure. Mechanism: the construction agent under-extracts superlative goal statements. This skill abstracts that gap by requiring extraction of any explicit primary goal. Applies to future sessions where a speaker states a personal top priority in any domain, but not to implicit or vague aspirations.

payload.name: Extract-Explicit-Importance-Preference-Memory
payload.description: When a user explicitly says something is important, valued, or a priority, apply during construction extraction or update to create or update a preference memory capturing that claim even if the same message also describes an event or action.
content: During extraction, if a message contains an explicit stated value or importance (e.g., 'X is really important to me', 'I value Y'), extract it as a separate preference memory for the speaker, in addition to any event or action memory from the same message.

During update or enrichment, when a later message restates or reinforces such an explicit importance, add it to the existing memory if absent; do not let it be absorbed into an event narrative where it becomes implicit.

candidates.solves: Diagnosed cause: the extraction candidate preserved the routine event but dropped the speaker's explicit statement that something is important to them, so the memory could not answer why the routine happened. The reusable mechanism is treating explicit importance/value statements as secondary to an event. This skill applies to future construction passes where a message declares a value or priority; it should persist that claim as a preference memory, separate from any event narrative. It does not apply to preferences that are only inferred, not explicitly stated.

payload.name: Extract reminder-linked personal values
payload.description: When a user mentions an object, image, quote, or practice as a reminder of a personal value, goal, or identity, extract that value as a preference or state memory.
content: During candidate extraction, if a speaker says they have or use something (e.g., a painting, photo, quote, ritual) to remind them to uphold a specific value or goal, create a memory of that value/goal as a preference or state.
Store the underlying value or aspiration (e.g., 'be a leader'), not just the fact of owning the object.
If a memory for the same value already exists, perform an UPDATE or MERGE instead of creating a duplicate.

candidates.solves: Construction agents sometimes skip self-descriptive statements where a user mentions a physical object or symbol as a reminder of a personal value or goal, leaving the underlying aspiration unrecorded. This skill guides extraction of such statements into durable preference/state memories, regardless of the conversational topic or object involved. It should be applied whenever a speaker explicitly links an object or ritual to a value they strive to uphold; it is not intended for mere object ownership statements or for values attributed to other people.

payload.name: Extract each explicitly stated goal as a distinct memory
payload.description: When a speaker explicitly states multiple goals, priorities, or aspirations in one message or across a conversation, extract each distinct goal as its own candidate memory instead of merging or omitting one.
content: During extraction, create a separate candidate memory for each explicitly stated goal or aspiration (e.g., 'my goal is', 'I want to', 'number one goal', 'also want'), even when multiple appear in the same message or turn.
Do not merge multiple distinct goals into one broader memory; keep each goal independently so that downstream reference claims can be matched.

Treat emphatic or superlative goal statements ('my number one goal', 'most important goal') as ordinary explicit goals and extract them even if another goal was already captured from an earlier exchange.

candidates.solves: Extraction may drop or merge one explicitly stated goal when a message contains multiple goals, especially a goal introduced as "number one" alongside other goals. The rule to extract each distinct goal as its own memory candidate is a valid general remedy for any multi-goal statement. It applies to future conversations where a speaker lists multiple goals, aspirations, or priorities in one message or across turns.

payload.name: preserve-confirmed-ordinals-when-extracting-events
payload.description: When extracting an event or profile memory from dialogue, include an ordinal qualifier (first, second, third) and the item type whenever the speaker explicitly confirms them.
content: During extraction, treat an explicitly confirmed ordinal as a core fact. If the speaker answers a yes/no ordinal question with confirmation, record 'third [item]' in the candidate content.
Do not add an ordinal when it is only a guess or not directly confirmed; record only explicitly stated attributes.
Include the item type named in the original question along with the ordinal and any thematic details.

candidates.solves: Extraction candidates often retain thematic detail but drop explicitly confirmed ordinal identifiers, making later queries about 'third X' unanswerable. This rule applies whenever a user confirms an ordinal in conversation and a memory is extracted; it does not apply to unconfirmed guesses or implied numbers.

payload.name: Extract explicit confidence and motivation strategies as preferences
payload.description: When a person explicitly states how they stay confident, motivated, or cope with challenges in work/business, extract those stated strategies as preference candidates during construction.
content: During candidate extraction, if a speaker explicitly describes recurring strategies for staying confident, motivated, or handling setbacks (e.g., 'I stay motivated by...', 'It helps to have...', 'I focus on...'), create one preference candidate for each distinct strategy. Do not skip these statements as conversational filler, because they are durable facts about the speaker.

candidates.solves: Construction ingestion can silently drop explicit statements about how a person stays confident, motivated, or handles setbacks, especially when they appear inside supportive advice exchanges. This rule ensures such self-disclosed strategies are extracted as preference memories so later questions about mindset can be answered; it applies to explicit 'I stay motivated/cope by...' statements but not to implied strategies or one-off actions.

payload.name: Extract spoken descriptions of shared photos
payload.description: When a user shares a photo in a message and immediately adds adjectives describing the subject, extract a memory of that description during construction.
content: During candidate extraction, when a message includes a photo and an accompanying descriptive phrase (e.g., superlatives or adjectives) that refers to a person, pet, object, or event already discussed, create a memory candidate for the speaker's description. Use the existing memory type that fits (e.g., preference or event), include the described subject and the quoted phrase, and do not skip it because the photo itself contributes no text.

candidates.solves: Construction failed because descriptive statements attached to image shares were not extracted into candidates, causing the referenced fact to be absent from memory. The reusable mechanism is that evaluative phrases following a photo often describe an object already mentioned in the conversation. Future inputs with photo-sharing and short descriptive wording in the same message should trigger extraction rather than being skipped.

payload.name: capture-explicit-sharing-events
payload.description: When a user explicitly shares or references a picture, photo, or artifact with descriptive details, extract the sharing event itself, not just the underlying object's attributes.
content: If a message contains an explicit sharing reference (e.g., 'This is my...', 'Here is...', 'That picture is...'), create an event memory that records the act of sharing, the item shared, and any creator/source details from the same message.
When extracting from such a message, do not only store ownership or static attributes; include the sharing action so that questions about what was shared can be answered.
If an existing memory already covers the object's attributes, still add or merge the sharing event to preserve the action.

candidates.solves: When a user explicitly shares or references a picture, photo, or artifact in a message, the extraction stage sometimes records only the object's attributes (e.g., ownership) and omits the fact that the user shared it. This causes later questions about the shared item to fail. The rule abstracts the need to capture the act of sharing/referencing as part of the durable memory, along with any descriptive details, applicable to any conversation where a user presents an item and gives its origin or description.

payload.name: Preserve Stated Social Relationships from Team Activities
payload.description: When extracting or updating memories from statements about team/group activities, create a separate relationship memory for the stated companions and do not let event updates erase it.
content: During extraction, if a statement explicitly mentions the person acting with a team, group, or companions (e.g., 'with my team', 'together with friends'), add a relationship memory capturing that the person has those teammates/companions, in addition to any event memory.
During CRUD, when updating or enriching an event memory, preserve any stated team/group/companion relationship unless new evidence explicitly contradicts it.
Before finalizing a memory change, check that relationship implications from source messages are represented as relationship memories, not only embedded in event descriptions.

candidates.solves: A social fact such as having teammates or friends was only embedded in an event memory and disappeared when the event was later rewritten. The fix is to extract stated team/group/companion relationships as separate relationship memories and keep them intact during event updates. This applies whenever a speaker mentions participating with a team, group, or other people, but not when no social relationship is explicitly stated.

payload.name: Extract support-object relationship memories
payload.description: When a user explicitly says an object, pet, or item helps them focus, calms them, comforts them, or brings them joy, use a relationship memory even if the item is a toy or stuffed animal.
content: Use a relationship memory when the user explicitly says an object, pet, or item helps them stay focused, calms them, comforts them, or brings them joy; this includes stuffed animals and other toys.
During extraction, always create a candidate for such explicit benefit statements instead of dismissing them as small talk or non-factual.
During CRUD, add or merge this relationship memory with the item's identifying details (e.g., name, type) and attach the stated benefit.

candidates.solves: Extraction under-generates when users explicitly state an object or pet provides emotional or functional support (focus, joy, calm), so the relationship is never persisted. A reusable rule should record such explicit benefit statements as relationship memories, including for stuffed animals and toys, while excluding generic compliments or statements without a named item.

payload.name: Carry forward established location context during extraction
payload.description: When extracting an event from a later message, check earlier session messages for a location already established for the same trip or ongoing context and include it in the candidate memory if the event is clearly tied to that context.
content: Before finalizing an event candidate, scan earlier messages in the same session for a location associated with the same trip or ongoing context.
If the current message describes an activity clearly connected to that established context without repeating the location, include that location in the memory content.
Do not infer a location when the event is not explicitly connected to a prior place or when the context indicates a different location.

candidates.solves: Diagnosed cause: an event extracted from a later message omitted the location already established earlier in the same session, so the memory could not answer a later question about where the event happened. The reusable mechanism is that construction extraction must carry forward relevant location context from prior turns when the current event is clearly tied to that context, instead of only using words in the immediate message. This applies to any future session where an activity is mentioned without repeating a previously stated place.

payload.name: Resolve relative time in extracted events
payload.description: When extracting an event memory and the source message contains a relative time expression (e.g., 'a year ago', 'last week', 'two days ago'), use the message/session timestamp to compute the absolute date and include it in the memory content.
content: During extraction, if the source text contains a relative temporal phrase such as 'a year ago', 'last week', 'two days ago', or 'yesterday', resolve it to a concrete date or year using the message's occurred_at timestamp and store that resolved value as part of the memory content.
If the exact date cannot be determined, store the closest approximate absolute value (e.g., year) and do not drop the temporal information entirely.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction often drops relative time expressions ('a year ago', 'last week') when creating memories, leaving event timing unknown. This Skill provides a rule to resolve such expressions using the message timestamp and include the absolute date in the memory, applicable to any event/purchase/occurrence extraction.

payload.name: Extract dated events from emotional narratives
payload.description: When a user mentions a personal event with an explicit year or date inside emotional or photo-sharing language, use it to create an event memory during candidate extraction.
content: During candidate extraction, when a user explicitly mentions a personal event (e.g., wedding, birth, move, graduation) with an explicit year or date, create an event memory with the event type and that date even if the surrounding message is emotional, nostalgic, or describes photos.
Do not treat emotional or reflective framing as a reason to skip extraction; explicit dated facts remain durable memories regardless of tone.
When the date is relative (e.g., 'two years ago'), resolve it from the message/session timestamp before creating the event memory.

candidates.solves: Construction failed because a dated personal event embedded in nostalgic photo-sharing language produced no extraction candidates. The abstract mechanism is that explicit event dates are skipped when the utterance is emotionally framed. This applies to any future message where a user states a personal event with a year or date amid reflective, grief-related, or memory-sharing wording, and it should trigger creation of an event memory with that date.

payload.name: ExtractUserPastEventWithTime
payload.description: When a user discloses a past personal action with a relative time reference (e.g., 'last Friday', 'yesterday'), extract an event memory candidate during ingestion.
content: During candidate extraction, treat explicit user statements about their own past actions (e.g., 'I made', 'I visited') as event memory candidates, even if they appear inside casual conversation or a question.

Resolve relative time expressions (e.g., 'last Friday', 'yesterday') against the message/session timestamp and store the resolved date in the event memory; include the action and key object in the content.

candidates.solves: Construction failed because an obvious user-stated past event (making a dessert) was not extracted as a memory, leaving the claim missing. The underlying mechanism is the extraction stage overlooking self-reported past actions with relative time references. This skill generalizes to any future session where a user mentions a past action they performed with a time expression, ensuring it becomes an event memory. It does not apply to actions by others, hypotheticals, or future plans.

payload.name: Resolve relative event dates during extraction
payload.description: Use when extracting event memories from a message that contains a relative time expression (e.g., 'on Friday', 'last week', 'yesterday') and the message/session timestamp can resolve it to an absolute date.
content: During extraction, resolve relative temporal expressions (e.g., 'on Friday', 'last week') against the message/session timestamp and record the resolved absolute date for the event occurrence.

When a message contains both an event occurrence date and a future plan/start date, keep them distinct: store the occurrence date as the event's date and include the future start as additional context rather than using it as the event date.
Include explicit date anchors in candidate memory content so downstream questions about when an event happened can be answered from memory alone.

candidates.solves: When a message reports an event with a relative day (e.g., 'on Friday') and also mentions a future milestone (e.g., 'next month'), extraction may drop the event date and store only the future start, making the exact occurrence date unanswerable. This Skill enforces resolving relative dates against the message timestamp and preserving the occurrence date separately from any later plan, so future 'when did X happen?' questions can be answered from memory. It applies to event extraction from messages with a usable timestamp, not to planning statements without an occurrence date.

payload.name: Resolve relative dates and preserve first-time markers in event extraction
payload.description: When extracting event memories, if the source message uses a relative time (yesterday, last week, today) or a first/ordinal marker, resolve the exact date from the message/session timestamp and keep the marker in the candidate content.
content: Scan each source message for relative time expressions ('yesterday', 'last week', 'today') and resolve them to concrete dates using the message/session timestamp; store the resolved date instead of vague phrasing like 'recently'.
If the message includes a first-time or ordinal marker ('for the first time', 'first', 'once'), preserve that qualifier in the extracted event content because it is a durable, queryable fact.

candidates.solves: Extraction often loses explicit event facts by paraphrasing relative dates as vague terms (e.g., 'recently') and dropping 'first time' qualifiers, making later date or ordinal questions unanswerable. This rule applies whenever a message describes an event relative to its timestamp or marks an occurrence as first, and instructs extraction to resolve and preserve those details.

payload.name: Preserve explicit timing in extracted event memories
payload.description: When extracting an event memory from a message that includes an explicit time phrase like 'a year ago', 'last week', or 'in 2020', include that timing in the memory content.
content: During extraction, if a source message states a time for an event (e.g., 'a year ago', 'last week', 'in 2020'), record that temporal detail in the memory content rather than omitting it while keeping entities and locations.

Resolve relative time expressions against the session/message timestamp when needed, but keep the explicit temporal anchor or its resolved value in the memory so the event's timing remains answerable.
Apply this to all event memories such as purchases, acquisitions, or occurrences whenever the timing is explicitly mentioned.

candidates.solves: When constructing an event memory, explicit temporal expressions such as 'a year ago', 'last week', or 'in 2020' are sometimes dropped while entities and locations are kept, making time-based questions unanswerable. This skill ensures such timing details are preserved or resolved in extracted event memories whenever the source states them.

payload.name: Extract_past_events_with_relative_time
payload.description: When a message includes a first-person past event with a relative time expression (last Friday, yesterday, etc.), extract it as its own event memory during construction, resolving the date from the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, if a message contains a first-person past activity or experience with a relative time expression (e.g., "last Friday", "yesterday", "last week"), create a separate extraction candidate with memory_kind "event" for it, even if the message's main topic is something else (like encouragement or advice).

Resolve the relative time phrase using the message's occurred_at timestamp to produce the concrete date, and include the activity, subject, and any companions mentioned (e.g., "with a group of friends"). Do not merge this event into a memory about the speaker's attitude or relationship; multiple candidates from one message are allowed.

candidates.solves: Construction agents often drop a speaker's passing past event if the message focuses on another topic, especially with relative time phrases. This Skill triggers on first-person past activities with relative time references (last Friday, yesterday), requiring a separate event candidate with date resolved from the message timestamp. Not for hypothetical plans, general statements, or third-person reports.

payload.name: ResolveRelativeEventTimesInMemory
payload.description: When constructing memories from user statements that include relative time cues for an action (e.g., 'recently', 'last week', 'just'), resolve the absolute date from the message timestamp and store the action as an event with its date.
content: If a message contains a relative time expression (recently, last week, this month, just, etc.) tied to a stated action, resolve the absolute date using the message/session timestamp and include both the action verb and that date in the memory content.
Prefer creating or updating an event-kind memory for such time-bound actions; do not merge them into a general profile with present-tense wording that erases the date.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause is that an extraction candidate lost the temporal anchor of a dated action ('recently joined...' on 4 Nov 2023) by folding it into a generic profile ('participates') without the date. The abstract failure is the loss of event timing when converting relative-time statements into memory. This Skill applies to any construction session where a user message describes a time-bound action with relative time wording, ensuring the action verb and absolute date are preserved in memory content.

payload.name: Resolve relative time in event extraction
payload.description: When extracting an event memory and the source message contains a relative time phrase such as 'last week', 'yesterday', or 'a few days ago', use this Skill to convert that phrase to an absolute date range based on the message/session timestamp.
content: During extraction of an event memory, when the source message contains a relative time phrase (e.g., 'last week', 'yesterday', 'a few days ago'), resolve that phrase against the message/session timestamp and set world_start (and world_end when the phrase implies a range) to the implied date range, not the message date. If exact day is unknown, encode the earliest and latest plausible dates from the relative phrase; do not let the message date become the event time.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction often drops relative time references ('last week', 'yesterday') from event memories, using the message date as the event start and losing true occurrence time. This Skill makes extraction resolve such phrases against the message/session timestamp and store the implied date range in world_start/world_end. It applies to future event extraction with relative timing; it does not apply to profile/preference extraction or to CRUD updates not involving temporal resolution.
